title: Tail bound for the off-center Fourier sum
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty family of subsets of the $n$ coordinate indices, and let $0<\varepsilon<1$. Suppose that $\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{6n}\right)2^n\le |\mathcal F|$, and fix a point $x$ of the sign cube. Choose a sign-valued Boolean function uniformly at random; then the probability that the absolute value of its prescribed Fourier off-center sum at $x$ is at least $\varepsilon$ is at most $4^{-n}$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a nonempty finite family of subsets of the $n$ coordinate indices
$x$ is a point of the sign cube
